meta.title: Conversation with Ayar Labs CEO Mark Wade on Silicon Photonics, CPO, and Next-Gen AI Infrastructure
meta.speakers: Ben Bajarin, Jay Goldberg, Mark Wade (Ayar Labs CEO), Jesse Leiter (Ayar Labs)
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · interconnect as the AI bottleneck · why optics is hard · TSMC COUPE bet · customers, timing 2027-2031 · funding and IPO path

snapshot: **Mark Wade** (Ayar Labs CEO) argues AI data-center revenue is gated by *interconnect* performance, and only optical I/O fixes the electrical bandwidth-distance trade-off.
Optics is hard because it stacks materials, devices, lasers, CMOS and advanced packaging; his optical engine uses a **3nm** EIC in the **TSMC COUPE** process.
Ayar is fabless and bets that photonics becomes a foundry-plus-OSAT feature, like HBM integration, by **2030+**.
Wade expects leading GPU vendors to ship CPO in **2028-2029** and the rest of accelerators in **2029-2031**; 2027-28 is a chaotic stopgap period.
Ayar's cap table includes **NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, TSMC** and now **Wiwynn**; total capital on the balance sheet topped **$650M**.
Market size: optics in scale-up is **tens of billions to ~$100B** per Wade; Ben cites **$30-50B by 2030**.
IPO intercept is timed to the **2028-2029** ramp; no firm IPO date is given.

themes.title: The interconnect is the wall limiting AI data-center revenue
themes.lead: Wade says copper's bandwidth-distance trade-off caps GPU scale-up, and optics inside the package is the only first-principles fix.
bullets: Ben: GPUs and even memory are scaling faster than the interconnect; "the interconnect is a wall".
Wade's claim: data-center revenue scaling is limited by interconnect performance in the **scale-up fabric** (tokens per second per dollar per watt).
Electrical links: the faster the data, the shorter the distance; optics solves it "from the ground up".
Optical TAM is **10-100x** the datacom volumes the optics industry used to serve; ChatGPT's release was the wake-up call that made connectivity-gated revenue a big enough market.
Wade's spreadsheet math: **tens of billions to approaching $100B** market; Ben quotes **$30-50B by 2030**.
Founded out of MIT in 2015; first processor-to-DRAM optical interface published in *Nature* in 2015.

quote.text: Large-scale AI data centers are limited in their revenue scaling by the performance of the interconnect in their compute systems.

themes.watch: Wade is the CEO and co-founder of Ayar Labs, a private company with equity from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and TSMC; the market-size and timing claims are his own.

names.name: Ayar Labs
names.blurb: Private silicon-photonics optical I/O chiplet maker (2, 4, then 8 Tbps chiplets); fabless.

themes.title: Optics is hard because every layer is hard and they must all work together
themes.lead: Difficult on difficult: advanced CMOS plus advanced packaging plus a new photonics process plus fiber and lasers.
bullets: Telecom had specialized firms per domain (laser, DSP, optical device); AI scale-up needs all of it integrated into one product.
Ayar's optical engine = a leading-edge **3nm** EIC with hundreds of millions of transistors, built via TSMC's COUPE process.
Adds to already-scarce CoWoS-class, multi-reticle advanced packages; then an optical connector must attach to the package.
Foundry photonics wafer "just isn't that hard": silicon waveguides, silicon nitride, germanium detectors; **fiber attach** is the hardest piece.
Current crunch points: laser manufacturing, production test architecture and wafer/assembly-level testing.
Wade is building a digital-twin manufacturing model with coding agents (a DAG with lazy evaluation) to optimize test policy across **five test insertions**.

quote.text: If you want to build things in this area, you have to be a bit masochistic.

themes.title: Betting on TSMC COUPE and a foundry-plus-OSAT supply chain
themes.lead: Ayar chose the TSMC route because optical I/O only matters at volume scale inside leading-edge packages.
bullets: Ayar has worked on TSMC COUPE for approaching **four years** and has "lots of wafers flowing" from the fab.

Ben relays whispers that TSMC is immature in photonics and that **Tower** and **GlobalFoundries** are further along; Wade says a photonics chip from another foundry works for pluggables and NPO modules but not for scale-up attach.
Ayar is part of the NVIDIA ecosystem, attaching to NVLink and NVSwitch.
Wade says finance people track progress weekly or monthly while tech progresses quarterly or yearly.
Ayar is **fabless**; Wade hopes for a rich foundry set in 10-20 years.
Success metric: how you build a product, supply chain and ecosystem, not the photonics chip alone.

quote.text: A photonics chip is nowhere near the final product form factor.

themes.watch: Wade is TSMC-invested (TSMC is an equity investor in Ayar) and speaks for a company whose chips are made on the process under debate.

names.name: TSMC (TSM)
names.blurb: Number one foundry; COUPE process used for Ayar's wafers; equity investor.

names.name: Tower Semiconductor (TSEM), GlobalFoundries (GFS)
names.blurb: Raised by Ben as alleged photonics leaders vs TSMC; Wade says their photonics chips fit pluggables/NPO.

themes.title: A chaotic 2027-28, then CPO rolls out 2028-2031
themes.lead: Leading GPU vendors adopt first; others follow once optical I/O is treated like HBM integration.
bullets: Short term: not in high-volume production, so customers scramble for **2027 or 2028 stopgaps**; everyone optimizes for time to the first revenue-generating token.
Wade expects exciting leading-edge GPU announcements in **2028-2029**, proliferation to the rest of the accelerator community in **2029-2031**.
Beyond **2030**, optics simplifies into a foundry-delivered advanced feature, ending the pluggable vs board-integrated vs co-packaged chaos.
ASIC-service route: close ties to **MediaTek, Alchip and GUC** let hyperscaler and startup accelerators integrate Ayar's engine at near-zero risk.
Jensen laid out a CPO switch roadmap at GTC, which prompted sell-side coverage on CPO for the first time.
Ben: we are far from giant clusters functioning as one computer; everyone is making trade-offs now.

names.name: Nvidia (NVDA)
names.blurb: Investor in Ayar; Jensen showed a CPO switch roadmap at GTC.

names.name: AMD
names.blurb: Ayar investor; among leading GPU customers.

names.name: MediaTek, Alchip, GUC

themes.title: Funding stack and an IPO path timed to the 2028-2029 ramp
themes.lead: Strategic plus institutional investors fund the path; the IPO is framed as following volume visibility, not a date.
bullets: Series D: strategics NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and TSMC plus two institutional leads, at a valuation Jesse calls "sensible".
Series E earlier this year led by **Neuberger Berman**, with sovereign wealth funds **QIA** and **GIC**, and crossover investors incl. Sequoia and Insight Partners.
Wiwynn strategic investment announced last week; capital on the balance sheet topped **$650 million**; Reuters reported a secondary.
Wade: by IPO the roadshow shifts from technology to financial metrics, with high revenue visibility from supply commitments.
At a Jefferies dinner, he was asked about test equipment vendors and probers for the first time in the US; public investors are getting into the weeds.
Silicon Valley VCs abandoned deep tech for years; funding came from deep-tech funds and public/crossover money.
themes.watch: Ayar is private; valuation, revenue and the IPO timeline are management's own statements and no figures were given.

names.name: Wiwynn
names.blurb: Rack-scale infrastructure maker; new strategic investor in Ayar.

names.name: Neuberger Berman
names.blurb: Long-only fund that led Ayar's Series E.

takeaways.title: Track optical I/O and CPO as a gating layer; GPU and memory scaling outpace the interconnect.
Anchor CPO expectations to 2028-2029 for leading GPUs and 2029-2031 for the rest; treat 2027-28 as stopgap noise.
Judge photonics vendors by foundry-plus-OSAT volume path (TSMC COUPE), not by photonics chip demos.
Watch Ayar Labs' cap table and IPO signals; strategics (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, TSMC, Wiwynn) are the tell.
Follow lasers, fiber attach and test insertion as the real crunch points; lasers are promised for a future episode.

hot_takes.take: We're so far away from giant clusters functioning as one computer, which shows how early we are in this process.
From a wafer foundry process perspective, silicon photonics just isn't that hard to do.
hot_takes.why: contrarian vs. everyone says it's hard

hot_takes.take: You can have the greatest technology in the world, but if you can't ramp true volume production, it's not a solution.
I think we're going to see a lot of exciting things from the leading-edge GPU guys in 2028 and 2029.

claims.claim: Leading-edge GPU vendors ship co-packaged optics in 2028-2029.
The rest of the accelerator community adopts optical I/O in 2029-2031.
Optical scale-up connectivity is a tens-of-billions to approaching $100B market.
The scale-up optics market reaches $30-50B by 2030.
Optical connectivity becomes a simple foundry feature after 2030.
Ayar Labs' IPO intercept timeline tracks the 2028-2029 ramp.

other_news.title: Sources referenced: Reuters (Ayar secondary transaction), Nature (2015 processor-to-DRAM optical interface paper), Jensen Huang at GTC (CPO switch roadmap).
Wade's side project: a coding-agent-built digital twin of CPO manufacturing, laser supply chain, TSMC packaging and test insertions.
Ayar has not yet covered lasers; a future episode will, and Wade calls them the other big part of the story.

glossary.def: Co-packaged optics: optical engines mounted inside the processor or switch package.
The high-bandwidth network linking GPUs and accelerators inside a rack-scale system.
TSMC's compact universal photonic engine process that 3D-integrates an electrical IC with a photonics chip.
Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider that packages post-foundry wafers.
Electronic integrated circuit: the CMOS chip driving the optical devices.
Electrical links lose reach as data rate rises, which optics avoids.
Near-packaged optics: optical modules placed beside, not inside, the package.
